newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Paranapanema clarifies delay in debentures payment.
newsitem.headline: Paranapanema clarifies delay in debentures payment.

text.p: Brazil's Paranapanema said it would publish Thursday a statement clarifying the delay in the payment of interest on convertible debentures issued by the firm early last year.
The statement was made necessary after Gazeta Mercantil financial newspaper today suggested that Paranapanema had to delay the payment due to its fragile financial situation.

"We will publish the statement to clarify that the payment was delayed after an agreement with BNDESPar. We did not postpone the payment because of a lack of money," said Helio Blak, the company's Financial and Market Relations director.

Earlier this month, Paranapanema had to pay around 14 million reais in interest to BNDES Participacoes (BNDESPar), the investment arm of Brazil's National Development Bank (BNDES), which acquired some 150 million reais of the firm's convertible debentures.

A total of 390 million reais in debentures convertible to common shares were issued by Paranapanema after local pension funds acquired control of the firm and other three mining firms to form a mining conglomerate last year.
The pension funds and BNDESPar acquired the debentures, but BNDESPar decided to hold onto the debentures instead of converting them into shares.

Paranapanema and BNDESPar agreed to postpone the deadline for the payment of interest on the debentures. Under the agreement, Paranapanema would issue preferred shares which would be in part acquired by BNDESPar by using the debentures to pay for the shares, Blak said.
The firm had 90 days to prepare the deal, Blak said, adding that now the company will renegotiate with BNDESPar how to handle the issue.
The Paranapanema group is made up of mining firms Companhia Paraibuna de Metais, Caraiba Metais, Eluma and Mamore (formerly known as Paranapanema).
((-- Fatima Cristina, Rio de Janeiro Newsroom 5521 5074151))
